function.label: Starting, Progressing and Succeeding: whole-pathway prompt
items: I want to get more out of studying {topic} in [subject]. Help me work out what excelling would look like for me now: ask me three questions about how I study, then help me set one goal about mastering the material rather than just the mark, name one pressure that knocks my confidence and a way to manage it, and put one strength into words I could use with an employer. Treat my setbacks as part of learning. Coach me with questions; do not answer for me.

function.label: Starting, Progressing and Succeeding 1: Articulate one's graduate capital for the move from student to graduate
items: Explain what it means to articulate my graduate capital for the move from student to graduate, and how it applies when I {verb} {topic}.
Explain how the ideas of graduate capital, transition and student to graduate can be applied when I {verb} {topic}.
Show me a short worked example of a student asked to {verb} {topic}, and how they articulate their graduate capital for the move from student to graduate. Label each move.
Set me a short task that asks me to {verb} {topic} and to articulate my graduate capital for the move from student to graduate. Wait for my attempt before giving any answer.

Here is my attempt to {verb} {topic}: [paste your work]. Tell me how well I articulate my graduate capital for the move from student to graduate, and the one change that would help most. Do not rewrite it for me.

Help me plan evidence that I can articulate my graduate capital for the move from student to graduate: graduate capital audit across Tomlinson's five forms. My topic is {topic}. What should a five-part graduate capital audit with evidence under each form and a plan for the weakest one include?

Help me plan evidence that I can articulate my graduate capital for the move from student to graduate: graduate capital evidenced in a real application or mock interview. My topic is {topic}. What should a submitted application or recorded mock interview, with the careers adviser's feedback and my revisions include?

Help me plan evidence that I can direct my own learning and development, as a lifelong learner: self-directed learning to close a career-relevant gap. My topic is {topic}. What should a continuing development record entry: the gap, the learning completed, a certificate or output, and how I used it include?

items: Here are the learning outcome, marking criteria and feedback for my work on {topic}: [paste them]. Help me read them as a tutor would: explain what the outcome asks me to show and whether the task is formative or summative, then help me judge my own work against the criteria, pick the two feedback points that matter most, and turn them into an action plan with one question to take to my tutor. Ask me to make each judgement before you give yours.

function.label: Finding and Using Sources: whole-pathway prompt

Then give me three questions to test each source for currency, authority and relevance, and tell me how I will know the main debates are covered. Do not list sources for me.

function.label: Criticality: whole-pathway prompt
items: Help me think critically about {topic} in [subject] rather than describe it. First ask me to sum up the main positions in the debate and who holds them. Then, for one scholarly interpretation I give you, question me on its argument, evidence and method until I can say what it does well and where it is weak. Finally, push me to judge which factors matter most and to state my own position, and point out where my stance shapes my reading.

function.label: Academic Writing: whole-pathway prompt
items: I am writing an assignment on {topic} in [subject]: [paste the question and my draft]. Do not rewrite it. First help me check I have read the question's steer and keywords correctly. Then review the draft for structure, argument, clarity and use of sources: show me where a paragraph lacks a clear point, where a sentence would be clearer in the active voice, and where a source speaks before I do. Finish with the three edits that would most improve it and a proofreading checklist.

function.label: Presenting: whole-pathway prompt
items: I am giving a [time]-minute presentation on {topic} for [subject] to [audience]. Help me plan it from the brief: what it is testing, a clear structure with an engaging opening, and accessible slides that follow "less is more".
